learning_objective: 🎯 Unmask prejudice through brilliant satire! Learn how Soyinka uses a simple phone call about renting an apartment to expose the sheer absurdity of racial discrimination.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: पेरोक्साइड (बालों को सुनहरा करने वाला रसायन)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An African man is looking for an apartment. He finds a good place on the phone, but to save himself from a wasted trip, he confesses to the white landlady right away: 'I hate a wasted journey - I am African.'

Instead of asking about his job or character, the landlady asks a shocking, ignorant question: 'HOW DARK? ... Are you light or very dark?' She is trying to measure his humanity entirely by the shade of his skin.

Instead of getting angry, the speaker uses extreme sarcasm. He pretends the question is highly scientific. He confuses her by using terms like 'West African sepia', mocking her obsession with exact color.

The speaker points out that a human isn't just one color. His face is brunette, his palms and the soles of his feet are peroxide blonde (light), and his bottom is raven black. He reduces her racism to a ridiculous color-matching game.

fun_activity.title: 🎭 The Sarcastic Actor
fun_activity.instructions: Read the poem aloud with a friend! One person plays the polite, overly-sweet but highly racist landlady ('Are you light... or very dark?'). The other plays the intelligent, sarcastic speaker. Notice how the tone shifts from polite to completely absurd!

exam_tips: 📌 Satire is the core of this poem. Soyinka isn't just complaining about racism; he is making fun of the racist landlady, proving he is far more intelligent and articulate than she is.
📌 Note the contrast between the 'good-breeding' (polite voice) of the landlady and her extremely rude, racist question.
📌 The line 'Wouldn't you rather see for yourself?' is the ultimate punchline—he invites her to look at his humanity, not just hear a color on the phone.
quick_recap: ⭐ The poem highlights the everyday, casual racism faced by immigrants in London.
⭐ The speaker uses advanced vocabulary to outsmart and intimidate the ignorant landlady.
⭐ The entire poem takes place in a public phone booth, emphasizing the speaker's isolation.
